metadata.title: A sharp lower general-position bound for Cartesian products
metadata.description: The lower general-position number of a finite graph is the smallest cardinality of an inclusion-maximal vertex set containing no three vertices on a geodesic. We refute the conjecture that the lower general-position number of a Cartesian product is at least the smaller of the two factor parameters. For every integer r ≥ 6, we construct connected diameter-two factors of orders 2r-1 and 4r+5 whose smaller factor parameter is r, while their product has lower general-position number exactly five. Thus the conjectured bound can fail by an arbitrarily large additive amount and an arbitrarily small ratio. We prove the sharp replacement gp⁻(G □ H) ≥ min{5,gp⁻(G),gp⁻(H)} for all nonempty finite simple graphs. The lower bound has a computer-assisted proof reducing arbitrary distances to equality patterns in the five-point pseudometric cone, followed by an exact finite obstruction check. The construction and unbounded-gap argument are elementary. An accompanying Lean proof verifies the fixed 11-by-29 counterexample at the level of actual shortest paths; it does not formalize the universal bound.
